issues.body:
Found cutting 1.3.1. #926 put `scripts/check_nightlies.py --only-when-releasing` inside the `release-build` job, and that job runs on every event: pull_request, push, schedule and workflow_dispatch.

While `main` carries an untagged version (the window between a release PR merging and its tag), the check therefore also runs *inside* the nightly run on that commit, and inside the push run. The only green nightly it can find there is the previous run, on an older commit. So it refuses, and the run reports failure: dispatched run 36347890771 on `7e695a58` failed only its `Release build` job. Both nightly lanes (slow, model-cache) passed.

Once that run completes, `check_nightlies.py` reads it and passes ("nightlies green at main 7e695a58"). So the gate is correct at publish time, but `main` reads red until the tag lands. That red is a false alarm, and one that trains people to ignore it.

**Fix options (owner's call):**
1. Run the nightly check in `release-build` only on `pull_request`. That's where it guards a release PR; publishing runs it by hand per the publication guide.
2. Make `check_nightlies.py` ignore the run it is executing in (`GITHUB_RUN_ID`), and treat "this run is the nightly on main's tip and its nightly jobs are still running" as not-yet rather than refused.

**Done when:** a nightly dispatched on a merged, untagged release commit goes fully green, and a guard test pins it.
issues.title: Release gate refuses inside the nightly it waits for: main reads red between a release merge and its tag

The 1.3.1 Exp 10 re-run (2026-09-27, big-mac-mini, `a1ba1e5d`, mistral-7b, `n_ctx 8192`) stopped early on **every** run, on bugs ledger D13's planning liveness (`planning_failed`, last=`unregistered_tool_proposed`). The August heartbeat ran 8 clean turns per phase with the same model and settings.

| Run | Turns before D13 |
|---|---|
| Exp 10 heartbeat, 2026-08-18/19 | 8 (clean, on the turn cap) |
| Exp 09 re-run, 2026-09-24 | 5 |
| Exp 10 re-run, 2026-09-27 (5 sessions) | 1, 3, 3, 1, 1 |

Records: `docs/experiments/data/rerun_exp10_2026-09-27/` (run logs included).

**What the logs show.** In session `20260927_110748` it is the **narrator** (`sim_orchestrator`) that fails, not the agent under test.
- The narrator's first `send_message` works; its reply takes 24 s.
- After its follow-up, mistral-7b answers each planning call with `sense_tools`. That is a tool on the AUT's registry, and the narrator has only `send_message`, `observe_actions` and `check_completion`.
- `SimAdapter.should_skip_fallback_proposal` drops each one as unregistered, and the loop aborts after four.
- The AUT's reply the narrator had just read was a `sense_tools` capability listing, and the stall prompt repeats "Last AUT action was 'sense_tools'". So the model is plausibly echoing a name it was shown.

**Open question: is this a regression, or a noisy model?** One run per date cannot say, and the model is stochastic. Candidates since August:
- #823 (2026-09-21): follow-up input construction. The tool result is now framed as data by `_followup_synthetic_input`.
- The narrator's stall prompt naming the AUT's last tool.

A cheap offline check: replay the narrator's follow-up input at the August commit and at `main` with a recording stub LLM, and diff what the narrator is shown.

**Why it matters.** Every Sim-Short re-run on the ledger (Exp 09, Exp 10) now stops after 1–5 turns. Exp 10's 1.3.1 re-run could show its per-turn gate on only one turn per phase, which is why its row reads "MAINTAINED, narrow".

**Done when:** the cause is named (regression or not). If it is a regression, it is fixed, and a Sim-Short phase reaches its turn cap again on mistral-7b. Either way D13's ledger row is updated.

## What
`tools/mode_switch.py::_self_grantable` (the #821 gate) refuses only a self-switch INTO a code-executing mode. Since #826, passive mode is enforced by capability at dispatch (`can_act_on_host=False` refuses the host-acting tools), so a passive agent that could call `mode_switch` could switch itself to `active` and step out of that refusal.

## Why it is latent
No runtime registers `mode_switch` / `autonomy_level` today (`build_tool_registry` only registers them when given an `autonomy_controller`, and no caller passes one). Passive→active self-switching was also a deliberate #821 decision, pinned by `tests/unit/test_mode_switch_gate.py::test_passive_to_active_still_allowed`.

## Decide with #922
When the approval surface (#922) exists, a passive→active request is naturally a human decision. Options then: make a switch that GAINS `can_act_on_host` non-self-grantable (routed to the surface), or keep #821's rule and document it. Owner decision 2026-09-26: file, keep #821 as is for 1.3.1.

Related: #821, #826, #922.

## Defect
Two outbound paths share #824's check-then-reconnect shape but were scoped out of its fix (owner decision 2026-09-26: #824 fixes the model-reachable path, `http_fetch`):

- **`utils/net.py::validate_base_url`** (OpenAI / peer backend base URLs) resolves the host with its own `getaddrinfo` to validate it, then the client resolves it again to connect.
- **`utils/http.py::download_to_file`** follows redirects (`follow_redirects=True`) with no per-hop address check (model and hivemind downloads).

## Why separate
These URLs come from the operator's configuration, not the model, and backends legitimately target LAN or localhost — so the threat and the right policy differ from `http_fetch`'s. The mechanism #824 added (`HTTPEndpoint(public_only=True)` → a connection backend that checks the address actually dialled) is reusable for whichever of these should refuse private addresses.

## Fix direction
Decide per path whether "public only" is right (downloads from a public registry: probably; backend base URLs: no — but then say what the validation is for). Where it is, route through a public-only endpoint so every redirect hop is checked at connect time.
issues.title: Security: validate_base_url and download_to_file re-resolve after their address check (#824 follow-up)

issues.body:
## Finding (design scope, plus an unmeasured hazard)

The bio-memory brief says "bias only widens EC recognition, never narrows" (`NAc.get_threshold_overrides`: `threshold = base − reward_bias`, clamped to `[0.1, base]`). **That widening only exists on the text surface:**

- `LinguisticEncoder` passes `threshold_override=` from NAc on both of its encode paths (`similarity/encoder.py`, the percept and decomposed-chunk calls).
- `SensorEncoder.encode_sensors` calls `ec.pattern_complete_or_separate(..., threshold=self.config.pattern_threshold)` with **no override**. Interoception, audio and world engrams never widen, however rewarded.

So there are two different engram regimes, and nothing documents it:

| Surface | Centroid | Widening | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Text (0.44) | running mean | yes, down to 0.24 at the 0.20 cap | a rewarded node accepts looser matches, **and each one is averaged into its centroid** |
| Sensor (0.85) | frozen prototype | none | a rewarded situation is recognised no more readily than an unrewarded one |

## Why it matters

- **Text: an unmeasured drift hazard.** Widening plus a running mean is the exact recipe the centroid-drift lesson warns about (0.40 collapsed 19 of 20 strings into one node). The fix there was raising the base to 0.44, but reward can lower the effective threshold well below that for the nodes that matter most. The brief's detection rule (measure isolated vs sequential) has never been run on rewarded nodes.
- **Sensor: a design question, not a bug.** Widening a frozen sensor node would pull neighbouring situations into a node that carries fear or want. That is a generalization mechanism, and it belongs to roadmap 1.4 Phase 5's keying / Rung B line, constrained by `docs/wiring/cosine-separation-is-directional.md`. It is not a quick patch: it would move every earned situation-keyed row (Exp 53b/56/60–62).

## Proposed work

1. **Document the scope** in the bio-memory brief (the widening invariant says text-only) and in the engram tracker. Docs only.
2. **Measure the text hazard offline**: isolated vs sequential EC on a rewarded-node fixture with bias at 0, 0.1 and 0.2, reporting cluster purity. If sequential collapses where isolated doesn't, the fix is a design choice: freeze the centroid on override matches, or count override matches without averaging them in. That choice gets its own plan entry, not a threshold tweak.
3. **Sensor widening**: no action. Record it as an input to the Rung B keying design.

Behaviour tier: learned (recognition bias).

Tracking: `docs/wiring/engram-formation.md` · Plan: `docs/plans/engram_formation.md` (item E4).
issues.title: Reward-driven recognition widening is text-only, and on text it feeds the running-mean centroid (unmeasured drift hazard)

issues.body:
## The defect

Two affordance annotators promise the LLM a learned-danger label that can never be produced:

- `tools/discovery.py::_annotate_aff`: `if bias < -0.01: return f"{aff_name} [DANGEROUS]"`
- `integration/bio_enrichment.py::_annotate_affordance_valence`: `if max_bias < -0.01: ... [DANGEROUS — learned from prior experience]`. Its class docstring advertises `"fire_breath [DANGEROUS]"`.

Both read `NAc.reward_bias(agent_id, concept.id)`. By a pinned invariant (bio-memory brief, `_reward_bias` clamps to `[0, max_reward_bias]`; a bias clamped to zero is removed), **`reward_bias` is never negative**. The `[DANGEROUS]` branch is unreachable. The LLM only ever sees `[effective]` or nothing, so an affordance that hurt the agent reads the same as one it never tried.

`discovery.py` also wraps the whole annotation in `except Exception: pass`. That is a grandfathered silent swallow, which would hide a failure here too.

## Root cause

Negative experience is deliberately not stored in `reward_bias` ("pain avoidance is handled by valence annotation on edges, not by reward bias"). It lives in stores the annotators don't read:
- `percept_valences`, keyed `agent|entity_class|failure_mode`
- `cluster_fear`, keyed on a world cluster plus `drive:*`
- edge valence

The annotators were written against the pre-clamp contract and never followed the move.

## Fix options, which need a decision before code

1. **Read the store that holds the danger.** This is only possible if an affordance name can reach its key. `percept_valences` is keyed by entity class, not by the affordance's substrate concept, so the join needs designing: which entity does an affordance belong to at annotation time? This is a behaviour change on the LLM path.
2. **Delete the dead branch** and fix both docstrings, so the annotation honestly says "effective or unknown". This changes no behaviour, since the branch never fires.

Recommendation: do (2) now, and open (1) only if a measurement shows the LLM path needs a learned-danger cue. The Tier-3 annotation rows were pulled from the 1.0 framing, so no earned claim depends on it. Narrow the `discovery.py` swallow to handle-and-log as part of either option. The swallow lint's per-function count allows removal but not de-instrumentation.

## Regression guard

- For (2): a test that a node with only negative experience annotates as unlabeled, pinning the honest contract.
- For (1): a test that a real pain on an entity's affordance produces `[DANGEROUS]` through the real NAc. It is red today, so it can land as `xfail(strict=True)`.

Behaviour tier: learned (valence), surfaced as a prompt annotation.

Tracking: `docs/wiring/engram-formation.md` · Plan: `docs/plans/engram_formation.md` (item E3).
issues.title: [DANGEROUS] affordance annotation is unreachable: it reads reward_bias, which is clamped >= 0

## Finding

The Cerebellum's motor-engram and prediction read side has **no non-test caller**. The docs describe it as live in production.

| Symbol | Non-test callers (`src/` + `scripts/`) |
|---|---|
| `Cerebellum.form_engram` | none. It carries `Dormant since 2026-09-22` |
| `Cerebellum.query_engrams` | none |
| `Cerebellum.observe_action_sequence` / `ProgramRegistry.observe_sequence` / `register` | none, so no motor program ever crystallizes |
| `cerebellum_modulator_factory` / `CerebellumModulator` | only its own module. `reactions/bus.py` notes the factory "never passes" a reaction bus |
| `Cerebellum.predict` | only `CerebellumModulator.execute` (above) |
| `EngramConfig.gate_tightening_factor` | never read |

The consequences are:
- Program read sites (`agents/memory_agent.py::_enrich_with_embodiment`, `planning/adaptive_planner.py`) always receive `[]`.
- The acting-coach cerebellum layer (`prompts/acting_coach.py::_compose_cerebellum_predictions`) is always empty.
- Forward-model prediction errors are computed from real readings but only reach `sim_cerebellum_train` telemetry.

The one live piece is forward-model *training* in `tool_bridge.py` (and its state is not saved; see the companion persistence issue).

## Docs that overclaim

- `docs/embodiment_guide.md`, §Motor Engrams: it says engrams "decay after ~2 days unless reinforced". No engram-specific decay exists. It also says they make "context modulate future motor execution", and no consumer exists.
- `docs/embodiment_guide.md`, §Program Executor: pain gates, a PainBus interrupt and 10% gate tightening. There is no `ProgramExecutor` or `execute_program` in `src/`.
- `docs/embodiment_guide.md`, §Cerebellum activation in production: "every SEM affordance tool now has a live Cerebellum backing it". False, since the factory has no caller.
- `docs/embodiment_guide.md`, persistence line: the default `~/.maxim/memory/cerebellum.json` is never written.
- `docs/skills.md`: "Composable capabilities are now handled by the Cerebellum motor program system."
- `docs/embodiment_yaml_reference.md`: "Entity state similarity for engram matching (Phase 1b)".

## Proposed disposition (not a wiring patch)

1. **Correct the docs now.** State what runs (forward-model training) and what is dormant (everything that reads it). Docs only.
2. **Declare dormancy on the read side** with `Dormant since <date>: no production caller` docstrings on `query_engrams`, the program crystallization path, `cerebellum_modulator_factory` and `Cerebellum.predict`. This follows CLAUDE.md's dormancy-over-deletion principle: callers stay intact, and nothing new builds on it. Deleting it would be the whim-deletion the principle warns against.
3. **Resurrection goes through roadmap 1.4 Phase 5, "A graded predictor (anticipation)"**, whose audit already names `embodiment/cerebellum.py` ("write live, read dormant"). Wiring `CerebellumModulator` in ad hoc would put an LLM-fallback modulator into the substrate-primary survival loop and re-stale Exp 60–62, so it needs its own plan and four-lens review.

No behaviour changes under items 1–2.

Behaviour tier: n/a (documentation + dormancy record).

Tracking: `docs/wiring/engram-formation.md` · Plan: `docs/plans/engram_formation.md` (item E2).
issues.title: Motor engrams and Cerebellum predictions have no production consumer; embodiment docs describe them as live

issues.body:
## The defect

`build_bio_stack` builds the Cerebellum as `Cerebellum(config=CerebellumConfig())` (`runtime/bio_stack.py`, Step 4c). `CerebellumConfig.persistence_path` defaults to `None`, and `BioStack.save_cerebellum` only writes when that path is set:

```python
path = getattr(config, "persistence_path", None)
if path:
    self.cerebellum.save(path)
```

So **no production save ever writes `cerebellum.json`**. The same builder *loads* `<persistence_dir>/cerebellum.json` when the file exists, so load and save disagree about where the state lives.

Nothing in `src/` sets a Cerebellum persistence path (grep `persistence_path` across `src/`: only the Hippocampus/ATL factories in `create.py`).

## Why it matters

- The forward model does learn on a live path: `embodiment/tool_bridge.py` calls `observe_from_action` with real `sensor.read()` values after each modulator executes. Every session throws that learning away.
- **Three call sites guard a no-op.** `BioStack.on_session_end`, `agent_factory.py` shutdown ("Review fix (Arch #2)") and `minecraft_harness.py` (executor-lens review) all call `save_cerebellum()` because the bio-memory brief's invariant says it "must be called at session end". The invariant's regression guard is the call itself, so it passes while nothing is saved. This is the vacuous-guard family: a mechanism that doesn't run looks exactly like one that ran and found nothing.
- `docs/embodiment_guide.md` states the default is `~/.maxim/memory/cerebellum.json`. That is untrue today.

## Root cause and fix

The root cause is two sources of truth for one path: the builder hard-codes `p / "cerebellum.json"` for load, while save reads the config. The fix is to construct the Cerebellum with `CerebellumConfig(persistence_path=str(p / "cerebellum.json"))` when `persistence_dir` is given, and let `load()`/`save()` both use the config. Adding a path at each caller would be a band-aid.

Also drop the `except ImportError` fallback in `Cerebellum.save` that hand-rolls `open().write()`. `atomic_io` is a core module, so the fallback can't fire, and it's a second writer.

## Regression guard (proven by deletion)

A test that builds a real bio-stack in a tmp home, trains one forward model through `observe_from_action`, calls `BioStack.on_session_end()`, asserts the file exists, then builds a second stack and reads the same prediction back. Delete the `persistence_path=` line and it must go red. Today it is red.

## Scope and re-run triggers

- Persisting forward models changes no behaviour today: `Cerebellum.predict` has no production consumer (see the companion issue on the motor-engram read side).
- No earned ledger row names the Cerebellum, so no re-run fires.
- `~/.maxim/` gains a file, so check `maxim substrate` export and the hivemind scrub. Bundles do not include the Cerebellum today, and that stays true.

Behaviour tier: n/a (persistence correctness).

Tracking: `docs/wiring/engram-formation.md` · Plan: `docs/plans/engram_formation.md` (item E1).
issues.title: Cerebellum state is never saved: build_bio_stack sets no persistence_path, so save_cerebellum() is a no-op at all three call sites

issues.body:
## The defect

`minecraft_player`'s world channel encodes `time_of_day` (ticks/24000, a **circular** clock) as a **linear** value in [0, 1]. So two moments about a minute apart, just before and just after dawn, sit at opposite extremes of that sensor. The body YAML already notes the wrap: 0.99 and 0.01 "embed at opposite basis ends".

**Measured offline** (the Exp 62 replay's own embedding, which reproduces the live gate cosine 0.7874): cosine of the sealed-shell pool-floor reading at each time to the same place at the frozen-day time 0.0417:

| time_of_day | 0.01 | 0.10 | 0.25 | 0.50 | 0.75 (midnight) | 0.90 | 0.95 | 0.99 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cos | 0.995 | 0.986 | 0.919 | 0.892 | 0.903 | 0.884 | 0.847 | **0.799** |

The world channel's completion threshold is 0.85. So the earned Exp 60–62 drowning fear holds through midnight and misses only in the ~5% of the day before the wrap (time ≈ 0.94–0.99). This is the "night pool 0.799" that the Exp 62 records called a night miss. It is the wrap, not night.

## Why it matters

Every day, the world state jumps between opposite extremes around the wrap. Anything keyed on the world channel (NAc cluster fear, cluster reward bias, 2S-b/2S-d situations) gets a spurious context boundary once per day, in the hour before dawn. It is invisible under the harnesses' frozen-day protocol.

## Candidate fix, and its cost

Encode `time_of_day` circularly, for example as a sin/cos pair of sensors (the YAML's own lever), or decide it does not belong in the world channel (it carries `rest: null` by design).

Either change moves world-channel geometry. That fires the re-validation triggers for Exp 53b/56/60–62 and the retrosplenial §5 registry (roadmap 1.4 Phase 5, "Keying / generalization"), so it wants its own plan and design review, not a quick patch.

## Found by

The two-lens design review of the Rung B SUPPORT pre-registration, 2026-09-25 (confounding + environment lenses, independently). That run was not built: both lenses showed it measured the wrong place and was computable offline. The records are in the linked docs PR.
issues.title: world channel: time_of_day is encoded linearly, so each day has a spurious context boundary at the wrap (the Exp 62 '0.799 night miss')

issues.body:
**Anticipated pain (fear) is paid out as real negative reward, and also leaks into episode valence.**

### F1: reward
- `proprioception/perceived_pain.py` publishes its prediction as `Reaction(kind="pain", valence=NEGATIVE, context=ReactionContext(agent_id=...))`.
- `runtime/bio_stack.py::_distribute_reward_from_reaction` pays `-intensity` for any negative reaction whose `agent_id` is neither `None` nor `WORLD_AGENT_ID`. So a *predicted* pain is credited as if it had happened.
- **Live on the `maxim --sim` orchestrator AUT path.** Every orchestrator sim wires `PerceivedPainAssessor(agent_id="sim_aut", pain_bus=aut_pain_bus)` onto the bus that `build_bio_stack` subscribed to.
- **Not live** in the Minecraft harness or the Reachy runtime.
- The 0.5 s refractory only rate-limits it.
- **It cannot extinguish.** The intensity comes from NAc's own confidence, so the prediction confirms itself.
- **Near-inert today.** The reward lands on a clamped surface that action selection does not read. It becomes live action learning once R4 delayed credit, or anything else, reads that surface. That is trigger (d) in the plan.

### F1b: memory
`hippocampus.capture_reaction` folds anticipated pain into `Episode.finalize`'s net valence. Through the lossy ReactionBus→PainBus rebuild, it also reaches `create_pain_nac_subscriber`.

### Impact
Unmeasured. The cheapest bound has two parts:
- one logged `--sim` run that counts anticipated-pain reactions against `pain_chain.distribute_returned`;
- a unit replay.

### Fix
Step 3 of the deferred nociception-layer plan, `docs/plans/deferred/nociception_layer.md` (#878). It follows step 2, which stores `PainKind` on the signal and the Reaction. Once the kind is stored, reward distribution and `capture_reaction` exclude `ANTICIPATORY`. The fix must land **before or with** anything that makes the reward surface selection-relevant, such as R4.

Found in the four-lens review of that plan (wiring + risk lenses) during memory-strength 2S-c (#848, PR #879).
issues.title: Anticipated pain is paid as negative reward (F1) and folded into episode valence (F1b)

issues.body:
Found in the #872 review rounds. Verified on `main` on 2026-09-24 against the real `bodies/infant_humanoid`.

## The defect
Cradle Act 1 (`simulation/arcs.py`, the fire-pit act) tells the orchestrator: *"When the infant approaches or interacts with the fire, use set_entity_sensor to increase arms.thermal toward 0.8. Do NOT narrate pain; let the bio-pipeline produce it."*

`set_entity_sensor`'s `value` mode writes `root.vital_metrics[sensor]` directly. For a qualified sub-sensor like `arms.thermal`, that is an **orphan key on the root**. The arm modulator's real `thermal` never changes:

```
SetEntitySensorTool.execute(sensor="arms.thermal", value=0.8)
→ success=True | arms.thermal (modulator): 0.0 -> 0.0 | root.vital_metrics["arms.thermal"] = 0.8
```

So on this path the arm never warms, and thermal pain from the arm's failure mode can't come from it. The tool reports success throughout.

#871 fixed the **`delta`** mode: reflexes now go through `embodiment/tool_bridge.py::_apply_sensor_deltas`, which resolves qualified sub-sensors and declared ranges. The **`value`** (absolute set) mode is still the old code.

## Fix
Route `value` through the same resolution as `delta` (`simulation/tools.py::_sensor_slot` plus the declared range). Fail the call when a sensor is missing, as the `delta` mode already does.

## Before fixing: what did cradle results rely on?
Fixing this changes what cradle Act 1 does: the arm starts actually warming. Before merging:
- Identify which cradle runs and behavioural-graduation rows used the LLM-orchestrated cradle arc (Act 1). The scripted `cradle_mother` feeding (Exp 52) uses `_apply_sensor_deltas` directly and is not affected.
- Check whether any recorded thermal pain in those runs came from another path (reflex keywords, the orchestrator writing a different sensor) rather than the arm.
- Re-run or re-baseline accordingly.
issues.title: Cradle Act 1 heat never reaches the infant's arm: set_entity_sensor value mode writes qualified sensors to an orphan root key

Found in the #872 review rounds (#870 / #871). Verified on `main` on 2026-09-24 against real `ComponentRegistry` bodies wrapped in `Embodiment`.

## The defect
When the target part is missing, `simulation/tools.py::DamageComponentTool.execute` falls back to subtracting `amount` from the root `vital_metrics["health"]`. It returns `success=True` and sets `fallback_to_entity: True`. Nobody checks that flag, so the call is reported as a response that happened (the #870 shape). What the fallback actually does depends on the body:

| Body | Health model | `damage_component(component="torso_missing", amount=0.3)` |
|---|---|---|
| `bodies/base_humanoid` | `health: derived` (weighted mean of part integrities) | writes `health = 0.7`. The `evaluate_failures()` inside the same call then **re-derives health from the parts (0.982)**, so the damage **vanishes**. |
| `creatures/wolf` | `hp: 12` | writes an orphan `health = 0.7`; `hp` stays at 12 |

**Who hits it:**
- Six shipped quadruped bodies (wolf, horse, cyberdog, giant_spider, alien_xenomorph and others) lack the `torso`/`legs`/`wing` parts their archetype's reflexes target.
- `reachy_mini` has none of the humanoid damage reflexes' parts.
- Any LLM `damage_component` call that names a part the body doesn't have.

## Direction (owner, 2026-09-24)
Damage should hit **both** the individual component **and** the whole body. The whole body is the **sum of all its components**, not a separate number to decrement.

The mechanism mostly exists already. `Entity.derive_health()` computes body health as a weighted mean of modulator integrities (`metadata["health_weights"]`), and `Body.evaluate_failures()` applies it to bodies that declare `health: derived`. Only three shipped components declare it: `base_humanoid`, `host_machine`, `creatures/dragon`. So the fix is about **making every body derive its health from its parts** and **routing damage to a part**, not about writing to `health` directly.

**Open design points for the fix:**
- **"Sum" vs today's weighted mean.** `derive_health` is a weighted *mean* of integrities. A literal sum, or a mean weighted by part size or criticality, changes the numbers. Decide which one "the whole body" means.
- **A named part that doesn't exist.** Should it fail the call (a retryable error for the LLM, `failed` for a reflex), or resolve to a default or nearest part? Silently decrementing a root number is ruled out.
- **Bodies with no parts** (e.g. `wolf`'s flat `hp`). Either give them parts, or make `hp` the derived quantity with a single implicit part. Same for `reachy_mini`.
- **The archetype reflex sets** should target parts every body of that archetype has. Tie-in: `docs/plans/deferred/reflex_layering.md`.

## Gates
This changes how damage lands on every non-derived body, and for derived ones it makes previously-lost damage real. Check the behavioural-graduation rows that read health or integrity (row 9 / Exp 09, and any creature-combat rows) and re-run them, or re-baseline them.

issues.body:
Split `sim_logger` into an output core and a presentation layer, by making the terminal a SINK.

## Why this is not just "move functions between files"

`sim_logger.py` (1810 lines) does four jobs: instrumentation emitters, sink registry + JSONL persistence, agent-nickname identity, and terminal presentation. Only the first two are what the bio layers call.

But the seam is inside the hottest function on the path. `sim_log` — the one every bio system reaches — renders the terminal **inline**:

```python
    # Build the display line
    ...
    display = get_active_display()
    if display is not None:
        display.log(subsystem.lower(), plain_msg, agent=nickname)
    else:
        print(line, flush=True)
```

and reads **seven** pieces of module-level presentation state to get there: `_display_tier`, `_SUBSYSTEM_TIERS`, `_debug_mode`, `_interactive_mode`, `_agent_nicknames`, `_active_display`, plus the trace state (`_sim_active`, `_sim_sinks`, `_log_records`).

So a file-level cut does not separate anything. The emitter would still import the presentation state back.

## The shape that does work

**Make terminal rendering a registered sink.** The mechanism already exists and already carries the console `/ws` bridge; the terminal is the one consumer that bypasses it by being written inline.

- **`utils/trace.py`** — build the record, dispatch to sinks, buffer, persist. No knowledge of tiers, nicknames, displays or interactivity.
- **`simulation/sim_display.py`** — registers a terminal sink and owns everything presentational: `DisplayTier` + `_SUBSYSTEM_TIERS` gating, nickname resolution, `InteractiveMode`, `should_prompt`, the `display_*` helpers.

The tier gate stops being a filter *inside* the emitter and becomes the terminal sink's own business, which is where it belongs — the `/ws` sink already receives events "regardless of terminal tier" (per `sim_log`'s own comment), so the gate was never about the record, only about the screen.

## This supersedes part of #865

#865 proposes moving the whole module to `utils/trace.py`. That is wrong, and this issue is why: it would relocate `display_scene`, `should_prompt`, `InteractiveMode` and the rest of the terminal surface into `utils/`, which is a worse layering than the one it fixes. `utils/` should not own how a simulation turn looks on screen.

Corrected plan: **split first (this issue), then #865 moves only the trace core.** The presentation half never moves — it is already in the right place, just tangled with the wrong neighbour.

## What makes it tractable

Once #864 lands, **no bio layer imports the presentation half at all** — `pain_bus.py` is the only one that does today, and #864 removes it. Every other bio-layer import is a pure `sim_*` emitter. So after #864 the partition is clean at the consumer level, and the only tangle left is the one inside `sim_log`.

The 22 modules importing presentation symbols (cli, api, interactive, runtime, tools, simulation/*, and `utils/logging.py` + `utils/response_output.py` for `get_active_display`) keep working unchanged if `simulation/sim_display.py` re-exports them.

`utils/logging.py` and `utils/response_output.py` reaching into `simulation/` for `get_active_display` is a real wrinkle: the "is a display attached" hook sits below `utils/`. Either that registry goes with the trace core (defensible — a trace module reasonably owns where output is routed), or those two call sites invert. **Decide that explicitly rather than discovering it mid-refactor.**

## Honest cost

This touches the function every bio system calls, on a path with no test that asserts terminal output shape. It is a design change, not a mechanical one, and it deserves the two-lens round before building — not a "while we're here" rider on #865.

## What would close it

- Terminal rendering registered as a sink; `sim_log` free of `_display_tier`, `_active_display`, `_agent_nicknames`, `InteractiveMode`.
- The `get_active_display` ownership question answered in writing, either way.
- A test that an event reaches sinks when the terminal tier would have hidden it (today's documented behaviour, currently implicit in `sim_log`'s control flow — prove it non-vacuous by re-adding the gate ahead of dispatch).
- Console `/ws` and `--display bio|clean|debug` verified end to end.

Blocks: #865 (its move should carry only the trace core). Depends on: #864 (removes the last bio-layer presentation import).
issues.title: Split sim_logger: make terminal rendering a sink, so the output core can leave simulation/

issues.body:
Move `sim_logger` out of `simulation/`, then let the architecture audit enforce the bio → simulation boundary.

## The situation

`simulation/sim_logger.py` is the system's instrumentation bus, not a sim feature. Reached from **40 non-simulation modules at 115 call sites** — `decisions/`, `memory/`, `proprioception/`, `embodiment/`, `runtime/`, `tools/`, even `utils/logging.py`. Its own `sim_log` docstring says registered sinks are "a first-class output, independent of `_sim_active`" (a terminal-verbosity switch), and the console `/ws` bridge consumes it with a process-lifetime consumer.

So the bio layers depend on `simulation/`. `utils/audit.py::LAYER_RULES` does not forbid it — there is no `simulation` entry in any ban list — and `architecture_baseline.json` has **zero** entries mentioning it. The edge is neither declared legal nor accepted as debt, which reads as omission rather than intent.

## Evidence gathered before proposing this

| question | finding |
|---|---|
| Does anything key off the module path or name? | **No.** No string references to `maxim.simulation.sim_logger`, no dynamic imports, no module-identity checks. |
| Does the module depend on the codebase? | **Barely.** 1810 lines importing exactly **one** thing from `maxim` — `utils.logging.log_swallowed_exception`. It is a leaf; it sits under `simulation/` by convention, not dependency. |
| Is the name in a contract? | **Yes, the FUNCTION name.** `console/openapi.json` + `console/schemas.py` document the v2 wire envelope as "the wire event IS the `sim_log` record", `kind` = "lowercased `sim_log` subsystem". The module PATH appears in no contract. |
| Is it redundant with `utils/structured_logging.py`? | **No.** That is the LLM-facing abstraction stream (`log_agentic`). Complementary surfaces, not duplicates. |
| Would a move close the edge? | **For 5 of 6 bio layers outright.** `memory`, `decisions`, `proprioception`, `embodiment`, `similarity` import only `sim_logger`. `imagination` also imports `simulation.entity_designer`, but **TYPE_CHECKING-only** — no runtime edge. |

## Proposal

1. Move the module to `utils/trace.py`. **Keep every function name** — `sim_log`, `sim_nac_predict`, the lot. The published contract names the functions; nothing names the path. Call sites change one import line and nothing else.
2. Add `simulation` to the bio layers' `must_not_import` in `LAYER_RULES`, so the audit keeps it closed instead of reviewer attention.

This deliberately does **not** split the module's four jobs (terminal presentation, agent nicknames, instrumentation emitters, sink registry). That is the tempting "while we're in here" change; no defect is driving it, and the front-gate rule wants a specific reason. Filed as noted, not done.

## Why the name survives the move

`sim_log("HIPPOCAMPUS", "...")` is the bio-narration that makes a run legible and that `--display bio` renders. CLAUDE.md protects that kind of vocabulary for the bio-system classes — names are load-bearing for the mental model. The layering complaint is about the *module's location*, not the word, and the two are separable. Renaming the emitters would cost a shared concept to buy an import edge that moving the file buys for free.

## Sequencing

**After #863.** A 79-file import rewrite landing on top of a 60-site swallow burn-down buries the half that needs actual reading. The semantic change first, the mechanical one second, so the move is reviewable by grep.

**#864 is independent and should go first** — it is the one bio → simulation edge that is a control dependency rather than telemetry, so this move does not fix it and it should not wait.

## What would close it

- The module moved, all imports rewritten, function names unchanged.
- `simulation` in the bio layers' `must_not_import`, with the audit green and no new `architecture_baseline.json` entries (if the ban needs baseline exceptions to pass, the edge was not actually closed — that is the check that matters).
- Console `/ws` and `--display bio` verified still working end to end, since they are the live consumers.
issues.title: Move sim_logger out of simulation/ and let LAYER_RULES enforce the bio boundary

issues.body:
60 call sites run their own logic inside a `try/except Exception` meant to protect against the telemetry subsystem.

## The pattern

#861 is one instance. `decisions/nac.py::NAc.predict`:

```python
try:
    from maxim.simulation.sim_logger import sim_nac_predict
    if result is not None:
        outcomes = [(result.outcome_signature, result.confidence)]   # caller logic
    else:
        outcomes = []
    sim_nac_predict(event=event_signature, outcomes=outcomes)        # the emitter
except Exception:
    log_swallowed_exception()
```

The `AttributeError` fires while building `outcomes` — **before** the emitter is ever called — and the handler swallows it anyway. The guard was aimed at the logging subsystem and caught the caller instead.

An AST scan of `src/maxim/`, excluding `simulation/` itself:

| | count |
|---|---|
| `try/except Exception` blocks whose body touches a `sim_*` emitter | **99** |
| ...that also run caller logic inside that swallow | **60** |

So this is a 60-site class, not a typo. Reproduce with the scan in the thread, or re-run it against `src/maxim/`.

## Why it happens

`sim_logger` is not sim-only. Its own `sim_log` docstring says registered sinks are "a first-class output, independent of `_sim_active`" (a terminal-verbosity switch), and the console `/ws` bridge consumes it with a process-lifetime consumer. It is reached from **40 non-simulation modules at 115 call sites** — `decisions/`, `memory/`, `proprioception/`, `embodiment/`, `runtime/`, `tools/`, `utils/logging.py`.

It is the system's instrumentation bus. The name says "sim", so call sites treat it as decoration and wrap it defensively — and the wrapper swallows their own bugs.

The repo already solved this correctly once, in `memory/layer.py::activate_after_use`: build the content first, then hand it to a call that cannot cost you what you already have. The telemetry surface does the inverse.

## Proposed fix, in this order

1. **Make the `sim_*` emitters contractually non-raising.** One guarantee in one place, replacing a 60-site convention — the repo's standing "push invariants into mechanisms, not convention" principle.
2. **Then remove the defensive `try` at the call sites.** This is the half that fixes the *class*: with no swallow, caller-side argument construction fails loudly.

**The ordering is the point.** Step 1 alone does nothing for #861, because that bug is upstream of the emitter call. Step 2 without step 1 would let a real logging fault reach a hot path. Neither half is useful alone.

## What would close it

- The emitter contract, with a test that a raising sink cannot escape into a caller.
- The 60 sites burned down (diff-scopeable; `scripts/lint_no_silent_swallows.py` already blocks *new* ones, so these are the grandfathered remainder).
- Each removed `try` proven non-vacuous the usual way: reintroduce a caller-side fault and confirm it now surfaces.

## Out of scope, deliberately

`decisions/`, `memory/` and `proprioception/` importing `maxim.simulation.*` is a layer inversion that `utils/audit.py::LAYER_RULES` does not currently forbid — it has no `simulation` entry, which looks like an omission rather than an intent. Renaming the module to something honest and adding `simulation` to the bio-layers' `must_not_import` would let the architecture audit enforce it. That is a separate change with its own justification, and `sim_logger` may be load-bearing vocabulary the way the bio-system names are — not to be decided inside a swallow burn-down.
issues.title: Telemetry swallows are catching caller logic: 60 sites, of which #861 is one

**Found in the memory-strength Phase 2c-1 review; systemic, not new to that PR.**

Adding a config section to `MaximConfig` without bumping `CONFIG_FORMAT_VERSION` creates a one-way downgrade hazard:

- a build with the new section writes it into `~/.config/maxim/config.json` on any `maxim config set`, while `_format_version` stays `"1.0"`;
- an older build reads its own `"1.0"`, so `is_future_minor` is False and the unknown top-level key is **refused** rather than tolerated: `ConfigurationError: config.json: unknown top-level key(s) ['memory']`;
- every `maxim` command then fails until the user hand-edits the file.

Verified in the reviewer's probe: `_format_version 1.0` + an unknown top-level key raises; `"1.1"` takes the tolerate path with a warning. The mechanism exists precisely for this and is unused.

**Affected sections** (all shipped this way): `console`, `tools`, `sim`, and now `memory`.

**Decision owed.** Either:
1. bump `CONFIG_FORMAT_VERSION` to `"1.1"` once, covering all four, so older builds tolerate rather than refuse (and check nothing asserts the literal `"1.0"`); or
2. state in `docs/user/configuration.md` that config files are not backward compatible across minor versions, and say so in the release notes.

Option 1 is the one the format-version contract was designed for. It was not done inside 2c-1 because bumping the format for every config file is a user-facing contract change that deserves its own PR and review, not a rider on a memory PR.

Behaviour tier: n/a (format contract).

**Pre-existing; found in the #847 review and reproduced by its probe on main and on the branch.**

`ToolPainBridge._pending_tools[(tool, invocation_id)]` is popped only by `record_tool_complete`, `record_tool_embodiment_failure` and `_on_pain`. A failure whose pain never reaches `_on_pain` leaves its entry behind **forever**. That happens when:
- the PainDetector cooldown drops it (for example, a repeat failure right away);
- the PainBus refractory gate drops it;
- no `pain_detector` is wired.

`_on_embodiment_pain` skips attribution whenever `bool(self._pending_tools)` is true (the "broad guard", which assumes serialized execution). So after one dropped failure, **world-driven embodiment-pain NAc attribution is silently off for the rest of the session.** Nothing raises; the agent just stops learning from out-of-band body pain.

**Fix direction:** the executor owns the invocation's lifecycle, so it should retire the pending entry when `execute()` returns, whatever happened to the pain signal. For example, a `bridge.finish_invocation(tool, invocation_id)` in the same place `_stamp_rpe` collects the RPE. This also stops the map growing without bound.

**Red test:** fail a tool twice inside the cooldown, then publish an embodiment PainSignal → NAc records nothing (today); after the fix it attributes.

Ledger: this touches embodiment-pain → NAc attribution (row 186 "ToolPainBridge attribution change" trigger). The survival rows' US is drive/threat pain through other paths; check which rows publish embodiment pain between tool calls.

Behaviour tier: n/a (defect).

The NAc half of #847. The #847 fix binds the tool-pain bridge's RPE to its invocation, but `decisions/nac.py::NAc._last_rpe` (written by `_note_rpe` on **every** NAc update: tool, embodiment, operant; read through `NAc.last_rpe`) is sticky in the same way. **Nothing resets it.**

**Consumer:** `agents/exec_agent.py::ExecAgent._evaluate_staging` reads it as `rpe_raw` for long-term staging significance at goal completion. The value it gets is the surprise of whatever NAc update happened last, which may not belong to this goal at all. If nothing updated since, it is the previous goal's surprise.

**Why it isn't in the #847 PR:** the consumer is different (staging significance, not capture salience), and the right binding is a design choice. Proposed: the maximum |RPE| over the goal's own invocations (the executor now stamps `ToolOutput.rpe` per invocation), reset at goal start.

**Red test:** goal A with a surprising outcome, then goal B with no NAc update → B's staging reads A's surprise.

Found by both lenses of the #847 review round (cross-confirmed). Behaviour tier: n/a (defect). A fix changes staging significance (D60's surprise heuristic), so it states the ledger rows that read it.

**Measured offline.** A ScriptedWaterBridge WaterTrial ran on origin/main 4a0362e2 for 14.75 s of full-loop time, with monkeypatched counters and no source edits. The script is kept outside the repo.

**Result: nothing in the survival world ever counts as memory *use*. The memory-strength plan's Phase 2 retrieval term is identically 0 on the benchmark.**

- **The percept gate is never passed.** `MemoryAgent._on_percept` ran 22 times, and **every percept had salience 0.0**. The gate needs salience > 0.2 (`salience_threshold`) or `has_maxim_keyword`. So `_begin_memory_formation` never ran, and `PatternCompleter.complete` (the pattern-completion function wired by `MaximAgent.wire_memory_hub`) never ran.
  - `PerceptionAgent.process_observation` derives salience from `state.data` keys `latest_vision_event` / `cli_input` / `latest_transcript_record`, and the survival path supplies none of them. Loop input goes to `pending_user_input`.
  - *Unverified:* whether other runtimes supply those keys via `state.data.update(observation)`, and whether live-bridge game events (incl. the new `--system_messages`) would.
- **The completer's cue can't match this world's vocabulary.** Called by hand on the run's ATL, it returned 0 predictions. `_find_matching_concepts` looks up `detected_objects` / `detected_people` / goal tokens by exact concept name, but survival concepts are sensor and action strings (`pos=0.64`, `minecraft_player_escape_water`, `drive:threat(1.00 →escape`). 16 of 46 concepts do carry hippocampus refs, so the material exists.
- **Bio-enrichment is built but never passed.** `minecraft_harness.py::_loop_kwargs` does not pass `bio_enrichment_pipeline=`, so the pipeline in `bio_stack` is unreachable there. That may be deliberate: there's no LLM in the action path.
- **Separately, loop captures carry no encoding signals.** In 38,465 saved loop captures (pre-#813, non-survival), `novelty` is 0.5 on 100% and `salience` is 0.5 on 77%. Loop observation producers (`sim_adapter.next_observation`, `environment.observe()`) never set them, so `Hippocampus.capture_from_loop` falls back to 0.5/0.5. #813 fixed only the MemoryAgent path.

**Why this is a design question, not a fix.** Lowering the gate, or injecting a fake `cli_input`, would be a band-aid. Making use and forgetting real in a substrate-primary world needs a substrate-native cue for retrieval, for example by EC cluster or percept id instead of by name. That is a new consumer, and it needs the plan's front-gate scope question answered first.

This blocks any survival-world validation of memory strength or forgetting, not the mechanism itself.

Behaviour tier: n/a (finding).

issues.body:
Found while mapping honest-activation consumption points for memory-strength Phase 1 (`docs/plans/memory_strength_and_forgetting.md`). Every site below retrieves memory for a consumer and the consumer **never gets it**. Each one is wrapped in `except Exception: pass/debug`, so it fails silently: a dead capability that looks like "nothing relevant was found". Same family as #841 (dead planner recall).

## Verified against real types (2026-09-21)

1. **B4 replan prior attempts are always empty.** `runtime/loop_state.py::_extract_episode_actions` reads `episode.content` (`EpisodicMemory` has no `content`) or `metadata["plan_actions"]` (nothing in `src/` writes it). The replan prompt's "Prior Plan Attempts — ALL FAILED" section therefore never renders on real episodes. `tests/unit/test_replanner*.py` pass only because their `FakeEpisode` has a `.content` dict.
2. **ExamineTool never recalls anything.** `tools/narrative.py` Stage 2 reads `m.context.goal`, but the field is `Context.active_goal`, so the `goal` read is always empty.
3. **Cross-layer knowledge context is always empty.** In `agents/memory_agent.py::_build_knowledge_context`, `atl.recall(name=record_id)` passes an ATL **id** as a name. ATL ids are UUIDs, so it returns `[]` (checked: `recall(name=<uuid>)` → `[]`). The branch then falls back to the confidence-sorted list, which is not seeded.
4. **Plan-failure recall raises and is swallowed.** `planning/plan_manager.py` and `agents/exec_agent.py::recall_deep` call `hippocampus.recall_similar(<str>)`, but the signature takes a `Perception`.

## Reported by the mapping pass, NOT yet verified (needs a JSONL sim run)

5. The PromptBuilder memory sections (`relevant_memories`, `concept_context`, `knowledge_context`, `valence_context`) may be unfed. Production builders pass `build_memory()` → `InMemoryMemory`, whose `build_context` has none of those keys. `MemoryAgent.build_context` is reached only through ExecAgent, whose `_build_llm_context` renders memories as `[source] salience` without content.

## Related, pre-existing

- `ATL.get` calls `touch()` under a **read** lock, which is a race on `access_count`/`accessed_at`. The plan's Phase 1 lock-discipline note already records it. Phase 1 does not change it, because it moves `access_count`, the default retention path.

## Why it matters for the memory line

Phase 1 counts a use only where content reaches a consumer. These consumers never receive anything, so they contribute no activation. When each one is fixed, the fix should also add a `MemoryLayer.activate(..., source=...)` call at its render point (the replan call is already in place). Fixing any of them changes prompt content, so the affected ledger rows' re-run triggers apply.

Behaviour tier: n/a (these are defects, not behaviours).

issues.body:
Follow-ups from the memory Phase 0 review (#813–#817). They were kept out of that PR.

1. **Percept captures count as successes.** `MemoryAgent` passes `result={}` for percept captures, and `Hippocampus.capture_from_loop` defaults `success=True` when no success is stated. A percept is not an action outcome, but it still gets the 0.7 retention floor for a "successful interaction". Fix: store an unknown success as unknown (for example `None`) and let retention treat it as neither. This feeds the memory-strength plan's Phase 2 failure signal, so it belongs there or before it.
2. **A plain `SemanticMemory` hit is reinforced twice per episode.** It happens once in `ATL.find_or_create` and again in `ConceptExtractor._register_concept`'s `elif` branch, which double-counts `reinforcement_count`. This predates Phase 0.
3. **The forming pool's run_id is `percept-{timestamp:.0f}`,** so two percepts in the same second overwrite one entry, and it keeps its old position in the insertion order. That makes the pool's "newest last" only approximately true. Key it by a monotonic counter.

## Defect
**The FearCircuitBridge has never reported a single event to NAc.**

`bridges/fear_bridge.py::FearCircuitBridge._report_to_nac` calls `self.nac.record_event(event_key, outcome, metadata={...})`. But `decisions/nac.py::NAc.record_event` has the signature `(event_type, event_signature, context=None, memory_id=None)`, so there is no `metadata` keyword and the second positional argument is a string signature, not a float outcome. The call raises `TypeError`, and the bridge's `except Exception: pass` swallows it. No log, no count.

Verified: `NAc().record_event("fear:x", 1.0, metadata={})` raises `TypeError: ... unexpected keyword argument 'metadata'`. A bridge report into a real NAc leaves it unchanged.

The bridge's docstring says it exists so that FearAgent "learns from historical outcomes". That half has been dead since it was written. It is the D43 pattern: a capability with no working caller. Found while fixing #839. Because of this bug, #839's truthiness fix does not change anything through this path.

## Fix direction
Decide what the fear circuit should write: an outcome observation through the API NAc actually offers for this, or `record_event` plus a matching outcome call. Call it with the right signature, and replace the silent swallow with a logged failure; the no-new-silent-swallows lint applies. Guard it with a test that a bridge report changes the real NAc.

## ⚠️ May retrigger experiments on fix
Yes. Once it works, the fear circuit writes NAc links it never wrote before. `FearCircuitBridge` is wired through `integration/memory_hub.py`, so check whether it is active in the survival campaigns (Exp 56–62, R3) and the LLM-path rows before discharging them. This is a behaviour change, not a crash fix.

issues.body:
## Defect
Tool results reach the LLM through the channel reserved for **what the human typed**.

`runtime/agent_loop.py` turns a pending `ActionFollowup` into a synthetic string, `[ACTION_FOLLOWUP type=… tool=… mode=… query='…']: <result>`, and appends it to `context.cli_inputs`. `agents/prompt_builder.py::_build_followup_prompt` then regex-parses it back out. Everything else that reads `cli_inputs` sees tool output as user input:
- `agents/exec_agent.py` uses `cli_inputs[-1]` as its **percept text**;
- `agents/llm_fallback.py` puts `cli_inputs` into its prompt;
- the memory agent's context and the sleep-state wake-keyword check read them too. A fetched page containing a wake word can wake the agent.

The reverse also holds: a user who types a line starting `[ACTION_FOLLOWUP` is parsed as a tool result.

Found while fixing #823. #823 frames the content at its source, so every one of these consumers now sees framed data, but the **channel** is still wrong.

## Fix direction
Carry the follow-up as the typed object it already is (`runtime/loop_controller.py::ActionFollowup`), on its own field of the request context. The prompt builder takes it directly, without regex, and `cli_inputs` holds only human input again. Each consumer then decides explicitly whether it wants tool output: the exec percept probably does not.

`run_agentic_loop` is under a function-length ratchet, so the injection should move into a module-level helper as part of the change.

Refs #823.
issues.title: Tool results travel as synthetic user input in cli_inputs (the follow-up channel is the human-input channel)

issues.body:
## Problem

A mode request carries no record of **who** made it. The model's `ModeSwitchTool`, a phrase heard on a microphone (#828), the CLI's `requested_mode` re-exec (#829) and an operator launch all arrive as the same string. That is the common root of #821, #827, #828 and #829. #821 closed one channel by hand-refusing code-executing modes. The design below closes the class.

## Design (owner direction, 2026-09-21: "start restrictive but move toward human authority")

- **A typed `GrantAuthority`, ordered:** `MODEL` < `AMBIENT_VOICE` < `CONFIRMED_HUMAN` < `LAUNCH_OPERATOR`.
  - `CONFIRMED_HUMAN` means a verified approval surface: #827.
  - `LAUNCH_OPERATOR` means a flag at startup: #829.
- **Each `ModeDefinition` declares the minimum authority it requires.** `singularity` **starts at `LAUNCH_OPERATOR` only**, which is effectively where #821 left it.
- **Moving toward human authority means deliberately lowering a mode's minimum as each surface earns trust:**
  - allow `CONFIRMED_HUMAN` once #827's approval surface exists and shows the triggering tool results;
  - consider `AMBIENT_VOICE` only with speaker verification plus a confirmation turn (#828).
- **The type enforces it.** Every mode setter requires a keyword-only `authority=`: `ModeSwitchTool`, `StateManager.set_operational_mode`, and the CLI seam's `_runtime_mode_switch_allowed`. A new writer that does not declare its authority raises `TypeError` instead of escalating silently. This is CLAUDE.md's rule on pushing silent no-op invariants into types; it would have caught the voice path automatically.
- **Time-boxed grants** (`CONFIRMED_HUMAN`) carry an expiry that survives the mode switch's re-exec (#829), and revert automatically.
- **Every grant or refusal is audited** with its authority and channel.

## Sequencing

1. Introduce the type and the per-mode minimum with **today's behaviour pinned**: singularity requires `LAUNCH_OPERATOR`, and the other modes keep their current rules.
2. #829: give the operator a real launch path (the `LAUNCH_OPERATOR` channel).
3. #827: the approval surface (the `CONFIRMED_HUMAN` channel).
4. #828: the owner decides voice's authority level.

Each step is its own PR with a two-lens review.

Refs #821, #827, #828, #829.
issues.title: Design: typed GrantAuthority per request channel, with a per-mode minimum (start restrictive, move toward human authority)

issues.body:
Follow-ups from the #822 two-lens review. They were kept out of that fix to keep its scope tight.

1. **Search ignores the policy's domain lists and page limit.** `tools/internet_search.py::InternetSearchTool` reads only `policy.enabled` and `request_timeout_s`.
   - `_filter_results` uses the tool's own `_blocked_domains`, not `policy.block_domains` / `allow_domains`.
   - The rate limit is `self._rate_limit`, not `max_pages_per_minute`.
   - Fix: filter results through the policy's list checks, without DNS, and use its page limit. Search snippets also reach the prompt; see #823.
2. **The operator has no way to reset the toggle, and the toggle tool is ungated.** The agent's `internet_access_toggle` is the only writer of `util/internet_access.json`, and its docstring says it "should require confirmation", but nothing gates it. `--internet-access` defaults to True, so it cannot tell "not given" from "on" and never resets the file.
   - Fix: gate the tool through the approval surface (#827).
   - Fix: give the operator a reset, ideally by moving the operator half of the policy into `maxim config`, the single source of truth. That would leave at most a runtime override, since declarative config should have only operator writers.
3. **`cli.py` records the launch cap as the internet state.** `state.data["internet_access"]` holds the launch cap, not the effective state. Record the effective `enabled` value instead.
4. **Push the rule into the builder's signature.** `build_tool_registry(internet_launch_enabled=...)` could build the getter itself, so no caller can pass a bare lambda. Today the CI grep plus a source test enforce this. That is acceptable, and this change would be stronger.
5. **NIT: the cached `InternetAccessPolicy` is one mutable instance shared by every tool.** The tools only read it today. Freeze it or copy it on return.

Refs #822.
issues.title: Internet policy follow-ups: search domain lists, operator reset / maxim config, gate the toggle, push getter into the builder

issues.body:
## Defect
Runtime switches into operational modes crash the CLI's re-exec.
- `cli.py`'s `requested_mode` loop re-execs with `--mode <requested>` via `cli_utils.py::reexec_with_mode`.
- `cli_parser.py`'s `--mode` accepts only `live, train, reflection, sleep, agentic, exploration`.
- So `ModeSwitchTool` → `passive` / `active` (the operational names the tool accepts) produces a re-exec that argparse rejects, with exit 2.
- Separately, `cli.py` hardcodes `_operational_mode = "active" if _is_sim_mode else "passive"`, so there is no launch path into `singularity` at all.

Found in the #821 review. The `--mode` choices were verified by the author. Since #821, `singularity` is refused before the re-exec; `passive` and `active` still hit it.

## Fix direction
Decide the one vocabulary for mode requests: operational names or legacy names. Then either:
- map operational → legacy at the re-exec; or
- add the operational names to `--mode`, deciding explicitly whether `singularity` gets a launch flag. That would be the human-grant path #821's design assumed.

Add a test that a runtime request to each accepted name survives argparse.
issues.title: Runtime mode switch to passive/active re-execs with a --mode argparse rejects; no launch path into singularity

issues.body:
## Defect
The Hippocampus capacity cap is silently exceeded.
- `Hippocampus._evict_one` never evicts long-term memories. If every stored memory is long-term, inserts past `HippocampusConfig.max_nodes` (10,000) proceed with no eviction and no warning.
- The config comment "not enforced in Phase 1" is stale: `_insert_and_index_locked` does enforce the cap, except in this case.
- Separately, `_evict_one` in both Hippocampus and ATL rescores every item on **every** insert at the cap: O(N log N) under the write lock.

From the 2026-09-21 memory deep dive (hippocampus and capacity lenses). The code shape was reviewed but no reproduction has been run; the fix PR should reproduce it first.

## Plan
Phase 4 (capacity) of `docs/plans/memory_strength_and_forgetting.md`:
- a byte budget set through `maxim config`, with a floor at today's values;
- lazy-heap eviction down to a low-water mark;
- over-budget handling that is loud rather than silent.

## ⚠️ May retrigger experiments on fix
None expected: no campaign approaches 10k memories. Say so in the fix PR, with the observed peak counts.
issues.title: Hippocampus cap silently exceeded when all memories are long-term; O(N log N) eviction per insert

## Defect
ATL compression is a one-way trap, and reinforcing a compressed concept crashes.
- `memory/semantic_types.py::CompressedSemantic` has no `reinforce`.
- `memory/concept_extractor.py::_register_concept` calls `concept.reinforce(memory_id)` on any hit that is not a `Concept` (`elif concept and not was_created`). A compressed concept therefore raises `AttributeError`, and that episode's concept extraction aborts inside the worker's warning handler.
- `CompressedSemantic.from_semantic` also drops definition, properties, `source_episode_ids`, `embedding_text` and `memory_refs`, and nothing ever decompresses.

Verified against `main` (class body and call site). The crash itself has not been executed.

## Plan
- Phase 0: stop the crash.
- Phase 3 of `docs/plans/memory_strength_and_forgetting.md`: reversible compress-to-gist. A compressed trace keeps enough to re-expand and to be strengthened again, which approximates relearning "savings".

## ⚠️ May retrigger experiments on fix
None expected: this fixes a crash on a path that only runs after compression (7 days of wall-clock time). Say so in the fix PR.

issues.body:
## Defect

Typed ATL relations share a single updateable slot per concept pair, so reinforcing one relation type can modify another.

- `memory/semantics.py::Semantics.define` maps every relation type except `CAUSES` onto `EdgeType.ASSOCIATES`. The real type is stored only in edge metadata (`relationship_type`).
- `Semantics.update_edge` locates the correct edge with `find_edge(..., metadata_match={"relationship_type": ...})`. It then calls `agents/bus.py::DependencyGraph.update_edge`, which writes to the **first** `(source, target, edge_type)` match and ignores metadata. The reverse update on a symmetric relation has the same flaw.
- **Failure case:** a pair `(A, B)` holding both `IS_A` and `PROPERTY_OF`. Both are `ASSOCIATES` edges, so reinforcing `PROPERTY_OF` can bump the `IS_A` edge's weight or metadata instead.
- **Why it's latent today:** `concept_extractor._infer_relationship_type` derives a single type from each category pair, so a pair almost never holds two typed relations. Anything that types relations from content (the language line, grounder changes) makes it live.

Found in the 2026-09-20 multi-lens review, and verified against the code: both the `define` collapse and the first-match `update_edge`.

## Where typed relations are used

- **Writers:**
  - `memory/concept_extractor.py`: reinforcement, plus `define_relationship` including `ALIAS_OF`.
  - `memory/concept_grounder.py`: Jaccard strengthen and weaken.
  - Unverified: `memory/episode.py` calls `DependencyGraph.update_edge` directly on the binding graph. It appears to hold `ASSOCIATES` only, with valence in metadata.
- **Readers:** `memory/concept_context.py` (LLM prompt enrichment), `memory/pattern_completer.py` (`EXECUTES_WITH`) and `tools/introspection.py`. All are wired through `integration/memory_hub.py`.

## ⚠️ May retrigger experiments on fix

The fix changes which edge a reinforcement lands on, so any result that reads typed ATL relations can move. From the review's caller grep against `behavioral_graduation_candidates.md`:

- **Possibly affected:**
  - Row 184, Wire-A LLM-AUT (PARTIAL): uses prompt enrichment.
  - Row 183, Exp 10 cross-session memory: only if its enrichment goes through `concept_context`.
  - Tier-3 LLM-dependent rows #11 (Acting Coach) and #12 (pre-deliberation).
  - Row 187, affordance transfer (PARTIAL): only if its proof of concept reads relations.
- **Not expected:** Exp 42/45/52/53b/56/57/60/61/62 and R3. They are substrate-primary, with no LLM in the action path, and `NAc.recommend_action` never reads ATL relations. The survival harnesses use ATL only through `activate_substrate_node`. Discharge them in the fix PR by citing that grep rather than re-running.

The fix PR should state which rows it re-ran or discharged, and add the ATL-relation trigger to those rows' **Re-run on:** field.

## Fix direction (root cause, not a special case)

Make the typed relation part of the edge's identity for updates. Either:
- `DependencyGraph.update_edge` accepts a `metadata_match` and updates only the edge that matches; or
- `Semantics` updates the exact edge object `find_edge` returned.

Guard it with a test that puts two typed relations on one pair and asserts that reinforcing one leaves the other unchanged. That test should fail on today's code. Run `tests/integration/test_memory_hub.py` as well.
issues.title: ATL: reinforcing one typed relation can update a different relation on the same concept pair

issues.body:
## What

The A4 gain law and `similarity/place_code.py` are individually correct and **mutually destructive**. Layering `w = (2|v−0.5|)³` on a population code inverts it: the most informative cells are silenced and the least informative ones carry the mass. For values between cell centres the whole population collapses to a near-zero vector.

Found during the four-lens design review of `docs/plans/world_channel_weighting.md` (2026-09-20), raised by the bio-faithful lens and reproduced independently.

## Measured

Through the shipped `place_code(value, prefix=...)` (default 7 centres, width 0.12) and the shipped gain law:

| value | top cell activations | → gain weights | total population mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.00 | 1.0, 0.0439, 0.0439 | 1.000, **0.759**, **0.759** | 2.518 |
| 0.15 | 0.4578, 0.4578 | **0.0006**, **0.0006** | **0.0012** |
| 0.45 | 0.4578, 0.4578 | **0.0006**, **0.0006** | **0.0012** |

Two failures, both from the same cause:

1. **Inversion at a centre.** At value 0.0 the two cells that are *nearly off* (activation 0.0439) draw weight 0.759 — 76% of the peak cell's weight — because 0.0439 is far from 0.5. Their combined mass exceeds the peak's. The code says "I am here"; the gain says "the cells that are barely responding matter most."
2. **Collapse between centres.** At a value sitting between two centres, the two *most informative* cells sit near activation 0.4578 — right at the gain's null — so total mass is 0.0012, effectively the zero vector. `encode_sensors` returns `None` for a zero vector (plan decision D2), so that reading encodes to **nothing**.

## Why

A population code's **activation already is the salience** — that is the whole point of the representation. The A4 gain assumes a scalar whose midpoint means "resting / uninformative". For a place cell, mid-activation means *maximally informative* (you are on the flank, where the code discriminates) and low activation means *irrelevant*. The two conventions are opposed, so composing them reverses the sign.

## Why it is latent today

`SensorEncoderConfig.gain_modalities = frozenset({'world'})`, and the only shipped place-coded sensor is azimuth on the **audio** channel, which is ungained. L11 recorded the symptom once in passing — *"a gained RAW azimuth zero-vectors the CENTERED reading"* — but as an observation about azimuth, not as the general law.

## Why it will bite

Place coding is the correct bio-faithful encoding for a **rest-less, cyclic** variable — head-direction cells, time cells. The obvious candidate on `minecraft_player` is `time_of_day`, which carries `rest: null` precisely because it is cyclic and wraps at midnight, and which carries 25.1% of the gain mass at the Exp 60 submerged read. Any future proposal to place-code a **world** sensor is a silent trap: it would look principled, and produce zero vectors.

## Fix (design, not urgent)

Gain must be **off** for place-coded cells. Options, roughly in order of preference:

1. a per-sensor `place_coded: true` declaration that excludes its cells from the gain (declaration-driven, matches how `modality` already works);
2. gain applied to the *source scalar* before place-coding rather than to the cells;
3. a separate modality tag for place-coded sensors, kept out of `gain_modalities`.

All three are front-gate-sized. None should be built until a rung actually needs a place-coded world sensor.

**Regression guard:** a unit test asserting that a place-coded reading between two centres does **not** encode to `None` under the active gain config — red today.

## Scope

No behaviour change is proposed now. This is a recorded trap so the next person who reaches for `place_code` on a gained channel does not lose a day to it.
issues.title: The A4 gain inverts a place code — informative cells silenced, between-centre values encode to nothing
